rulings.challenge_claim: A recurrence labelled byte-true shares no byte-identical material beyond the negative particle and is quoted in English only, and the frame form the back seam leans on sits mid-verse rather than closing anything.
rulings.grounds: UPHELD on both legs, and the second is sharper than the challenge puts it. Leg 1, the naming echo, upheld: the row's strongest_rejected_alternative calls the pairing 'a byte-true lexical echo straddling this row's own front seam' and quotes no Hebrew for it at all. The bytes give לֹֽא נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ (oshb:Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19, the split verse's FIRST half, the never-ruled/not-called clause; byte tier) against לֹֽא קֹרָ֥א בִשְׁמִֽי (oshb:Isa.65.1, byte tier). The verbal forms differ by a prefixed nun and by their pointing and the naming element differs (suffixed noun against preposition-plus-suffix), so the longest byte-identical run the two clauses share is the negative particle לֹֽא alone. At consonantal tier the shared material is two three-letter roots -- the call root and the name root -- and nothing longer contiguous. The echo is REAL and worth the disclosure it gets; 'byte-true' is a tier mislabel on the recurrence claim, on the one field where the campaign mandates a rival disclosure, and with no Hebrew quoted a reader cannot check it. Leg 2, the back-seam frame role, upheld and RESTATED more strongly. The row says the indictment 'runs to a closing divine-speech signature', אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.65.7, byte tier). That form stands at tokens 5-6 of that verse's 19, immediately after עֲ֠וֺנֹתֵיכֶם וַעֲוֺנֹ֨ת אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֤ם יַחְדָּו֙ and immediately before the relative clause אֲשֶׁ֤ר קִטְּרוּ֙ (byte tier) -- an intra-sentential attribution, as the challenge says. But the stronger fact the challenge does not state is positional: MOST of the indictment stands AFTER the formula, not before it -- the incense-and-reproach clauses at tokens 7-13 and the measuring clause וּמַדֹּתִ֧י פְעֻלָּתָ֛ם (byte tier) at tokens 14-15 all follow it. So 'runs to' is byte-false about the shape of the verse, not merely about the formula's role. The row is not blind to this (its own prose narrates the measuring clause coming 'after'), which is why this is a frame-role and positional overstatement rather than a fabricated signal. NEW FINDING sharpening the same leg: the formula stands at 3 verses in this chapter (sweep: 3 verses carrying the amar-YHWH form in any position -- oshb:Isa.65.7, oshb:Isa.65.8, oshb:Isa.65.25) and at exactly 1 of them verse-finally (sweep: 1 verse chapter-wide, oshb:Isa.65.25, byte tier). Of the three, the row picks the ONLY one that is neither verse-final nor frame-initial -- oshb:Isa.65.8's instance opens the koh-amar frame -- so a closing-signature reading was available in the chapter and this is not it. The seam itself is not in doubt and is not challenged: the koh-amar onset at oshb:Isa.65.8 and the mark layer carry it. Verified clean and credited: the ketiv/qere notes at MT 65:4 and MT 65:7 are inventory-true with the doubled tokens visible in the bytes, the bracketing parashah segs at MT 64:11 (= web:Isa.64.12) and MT 65:7 are inventory-true and correctly typed, and -- checked because this row reaches into the offset zone -- the split-verse reference is COMPLIANT: the refs carry the Masoretic-side dual and the prose identifies the first half by its content, which the two-zone rule accepts.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: re-tier the naming echo. Splice both clauses, state that the shared byte material is the negative particle alone and that the echo is a ROOT-level tie on two roots (call, name), and keep the merge refusal, which does not depend on the tier. Any reference to the split verse in that field keeps its dual and its which-half wording. boundary_rationale: drop 'runs to a closing divine-speech signature'. State the attribution's actual position (tokens 5-6 of 19, before the relative clause, with the incense, reproach and measuring clauses following it) and re-ground the back seam on what carries it -- the koh-amar frame onset at oshb:Isa.65.8 -- with the parashah seg at MT 65:7 kept as tier-3 corroboration. If a closing signature is wanted as a device note, the chapter's verse-final instance is at oshb:Isa.65.25, outside this span. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-read oshb:Isa.65.7's 19 tokens and confirm no field places the indictment's close at the attribution formula; and re-collate the two naming clauses AGAINST EACH OTHER, not each against its own verse, so the tier named for the recurrence is the tier collation returns. No span change; the 65:1 referent question stays the row's own held frontier item.

rulings.challenge_claim: The frame onset and the internal-pivot rejection are byte-exact, but the servant term the unit_type rests on is never quoted in Hebrew and runs straight across the row's own back seam undisclosed, as does the election term.
rulings.grounds: UPHELD, at the challenge's own low severity, with one wording correction. The confirmations are byte-true: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.65.8, byte tier) is verse-initial and the speaker named in the formula is יְהוָ֗ה -- a DIVINE frame, not one of the four royal-messenger sites -- and the pivot verse opens וְאַתֶּם֙ עֹזְבֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.65.11, byte tier) with no competing frame form, so refusing to cut at the second-person pivot is byte-supported. The disclosure defect is real. The unit_type ground is stated as the preservation of 'my servants' in English only, with no spliced form and no tier, on a field the operative-category rule makes load-bearing. And the token does not stop at the row's back seam: עֲבָדַ֔י (oshb:Isa.65.8) and וַעֲבָדַ֖י (oshb:Isa.65.9) inside the span, then עֲבָדַ֤י and its two byte-identical neighbours at oshb:Isa.65.13, one more at oshb:Isa.65.14, and וְלַעֲבָדָ֥יו at oshb:Isa.65.15 beyond it (sweep: 5 verses in this chapter, 7 tokens, skeleton tier -- the swept object is the chapter's suffixed servant token, not the book census, since the bare consonantal needle is a contained-form trap). The election term crosses the same way: בְחִירַ֔י (oshb:Isa.65.9), לִבְחִירַ֔י (oshb:Isa.65.15), בְחִירָֽי (oshb:Isa.65.22) (sweep: 3 verses in this chapter, skeleton tier). Neither chain is named and no unit-level continuity disclosure stands in for the omission. Both digits re-derive exactly. CORRECTION to the challenge's wording, not to its finding: its closing sentence calls this 'a byte-recurring catchword'. Across THIS row's own back seam the recurrence is NOT byte tier -- oshb:Isa.65.9's vav-prefixed form against oshb:Isa.65.13's differently-accented form share only the skeleton -- and the challenge's own tier citations say skeleton. It is an internal slip in the prose, and it matters only because a tier word is exactly what this item is charging the row with getting wrong. SEVERITY: low is right and should stay low. Both of this row's edges are strongly carried -- a verse-initial divine koh-amar frame at oshb:Isa.65.8, the petuchah at MT 65:12, and a second verse-initial koh-amar frame opening at oshb:Isa.65.13 -- so the catchword is a disclosure duty, not a threat to the cut. The challenge says as much and does not contest the cut. Verified clean and credited: the front-seam parashah seg at MT 65:7 and the closing petuchah at MT 65:12 are inventory-true with the two mark types correctly kept apart, and the paseq site at MT 65:8 is inventory-true with no position asserted (sweep: 1 parashah seg, 1 paseq seg, 0 ketiv/qere notes over the span's 5 Masoretic verses).
rulings.remedy: device_notes: quote the servant term from oshb:Isa.65.8 with its tier where the unit_type ground is stated, replacing the English-only 'my servants', and add a one-sentence cross-seam disclosure that the servant chain and the election chain both continue past this unit's close into the following oracle -- naming the tier as SKELETON across the seam, not byte, and naming each swept object (7 suffixed servant tokens over 5 verses in the chapter; 3 election verses). boundary_rationale: no change needed to the cut or its warrant. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-run the cross-seam cohesion read over oshb:Isa.65.8-Isa.65.15 and confirm no recurring token crossing this row's back seam is left unnamed, and that every tier word written matches what collation returns for the pair actually crossing the seam. No span change, no confidence change, no unit_type change.

rulings.challenge_claim: The fourfold formula that carries this unit is argued wholly from the English with no Hebrew and no tier, and the back seam the row defends is crossed by a byte-identical noun and a causal connector the rival never engages.
rulings.grounds: UPHELD on both legs. Confirmed first, and it is the row's strongest point: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (oshb:Isa.65.13, byte tier) is verse-initial, and the divine-title contrast the row draws is byte-true -- the earlier frame names the bare divine name at oshb:Isa.65.8 where this one names the stacked adonai-plus-divine-name title. Both are divine-frame sites, neither is one of the four royal-messenger sites. Leg 1 upheld: the formula that carries the unit is stated only in English. The recurrence is genuine and its digits re-derive exactly -- הִנֵּ֨ה עֲבָדַ֤י once and הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י three times over oshb:Isa.65.13-Isa.65.14 (sweep: 4 occurrences in 2 verses; 3 of the 4 byte-identical to each other, all 4 identical at skeleton tier) -- but the row supplies no spliced form and no tier, only a bare verse digit. Under the engagement rule a boundary-relevant original-language claim carries its pointed splice and its tier, and here the formula IS the unit's structural spine, so the omission is at the load-bearing point rather than at the margin. Leg 2 upheld, and it is the more consequential: the rival is rejected on subject-change alone, and the bytes contest that seam twice. הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.65.16, byte tier) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier) -- sweep: 2 verses book-wide at that pointed form -- a byte-true device straddling the row's own back seam, undisclosed, with the semantics running with it from troubles forgotten to former things not remembered. And the next verse opens on the connector כִּֽי (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier), which subordinates rather than opens. Under the standing cross-seam rule a byte-true device straddling a row's own seam argues continuity against it unless disclosed; nothing is disclosed. The election token crosses the same seam (oshb:Isa.65.15 to oshb:Isa.65.22, skeleton tier). NEW FINDING (not in either lens): the row's paseq citation names a COUNT-ONLY layer without its count. The inventory records 2 paseq segs at MT 65:13, and the row cites it as 'a count-layer segment' -- the identical template it uses at a 1-seg site in the neighbouring unit (MT 65:8). No position is asserted, so the WARN arm is not tripped and the citation is not false; but a layer whose only citable content IS the count is cited without the count, which is the count-object discipline applied to the one place it fully bites. Not challenged: the front-seam petuchah at MT 65:12 is inventory-true and correctly typed (sweep: 0 parashah segs interior, 2 paseq segs, 0 ketiv/qere notes over the span's 4 Masoretic verses), and the cut itself is not contested.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale and device_notes: splice the fourfold formula from oshb:Isa.65.13 and oshb:Isa.65.14 and tier it exactly -- 4 occurrences over 2 verses, 3 of the 4 byte-identical to each other, all 4 skeleton-identical -- replacing the English-only statement while keeping the existing verse digit. strongest_rejected_alternative: add the cross-seam disclosure the rival currently lacks -- the byte-identical former-things noun standing on both sides of the back seam (oshb:Isa.65.16 / oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier, sweep: 2 verses book-wide) and the verse-initial subordinating connector opening the next verse -- and re-argue the refusal to extend against those facts rather than on subject-change alone. The election-token crossing gets the same one-line disclosure at skeleton tier. boundary_evidence_refs: give the paseq citation its count (2 segs at the Masoretic key), keeping single-witness and no position asserted. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-collate the former-things pair across the seam and confirm the row now names a byte-tier device it previously left silent; and confirm every count-only citation in the row carries a digit. No span change proposed -- extending past the back seam is a boundary question and therefore a boss-adoption proposal, never author work.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the closing seam claim -- that the next chapter opens a new koh-amar frame -- is asserted only in prose without the quoted, tier-labeled Hebrew the row supplies for its own opening claim, and the row truncates its closing quotation immediately before that verse's own postpositive divine-speech signature. OL: the row's own quoted onset run begins with a causal connector and repeats a byte-identical noun from the preceding verse yet is argued as a subject-and-register shift, while the unit's one genuine closing frame form is left unquoted under a tier-3 mark.
rulings.grounds: The two lenses CONVERGE on two defects and OL adds two the LF item does not reach; all four are byte-confirmed. SAME DEFECT (both), upheld: the closing seam is argued from the next chapter's frame in English only. כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.66.1, byte tier) is verse-initial and is a divine frame, so the underlying seam is sound -- but the row never quotes or tiers it, unlike its own opening claim, which properly splices and tiers the new-creation declaration. SAME DEFECT (both), upheld: the row truncates its closing quotation of its own final verse immediately before that verse's postpositive signature, אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.65.25, byte tier, tokens 19-20, verse-final). The English witness runs past the row's cut to a closing attribution, so the row's own strongest closing signal -- a tier-1 form, and the chapter's ONLY verse-final instance of it (sweep: 1 verse chapter-wide; 3 verses carry the form in any position) -- is left entirely undisclosed while the close leans on a tier-3 single-witness mark instead. Both lenses find the same thing on the same bytes. DISTINCT (OL only), upheld, and this is where the row is actually weak -- the FRONT seam. The row's own quoted onset run opens on כִּֽי (oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier), a connector that subordinates this verse to what precedes it, and the noun הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת later in that same verse is BYTE-IDENTICAL to הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת at oshb:Isa.65.16 (sweep: 2 verses book-wide at that pointed form, byte tier). Both argue continuity across the seam and neither is disclosed. The row's 'front-seam unmarked' statement is inventory-true for the parashah layer, but an absence in a tier-3 single-witness layer cannot stand in for the tier-1 evidence that is present in the letter bytes and pointing the other way. DISTINCT (OL only), upheld: the rival rejection's tier and form label both overstate. The creating form is a participle unchanged across הִנְנִ֥י בוֹרֵ֛א (oshb:Isa.65.17), אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֣י בוֹרֵ֑א and כִּי֩ הִנְנִ֨י בוֹרֵ֧א (oshb:Isa.65.18), with the person supplied each time by an attached or independent pronoun; the three runs are SKELETON-identical, not byte-identical. So 'the same first-person creation verb' is a form-class claim the participle does not carry, and no morphology layer is staged, which means it needs the pointed-bytes argument it does not get. SCOPE NOTE on the LF item: it is correct and its own text concedes the claim 'checks out against the inventory' -- it is a register finding about missing quoted forms. It does not reach the front seam, which is the row's real exposure. Reading the two items together, the register gaps are the smaller half. NEW FINDING (neither lens): CONFIDENCE. The row records high while its own front seam is, by the row's own statement, parashah-unmarked, is opened by a subordinating connector, and is crossed by a byte-identical catchword whose semantics run straight through it. High is not carried by those bytes.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: splice and tier the next chapter's frame form where the closing seam is argued, matching the treatment the row already gives its own opening declaration; and extend the closing quotation of the row's own final verse through the postpositive signature, splicing and tiering that form so the close rests on the tier-1 signal standing in the verse rather than on the tier-3 mark alone. Add the front-seam disclosure the row lacks: the onset verse opens on a subordinating connector and repeats a byte-identical noun from the immediately preceding verse (oshb:Isa.65.16 / oshb:Isa.65.17, byte tier, sweep: 2 verses book-wide); state both, and re-argue the subject-and-register shift against them rather than around them. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-tier the resumption -- the creation participle is skeleton-identical across oshb:Isa.65.17-Isa.65.18, not byte-identical -- and drop 'first-person creation verb' as a form label, since the person is carried by the pronoun and no morphology layer is staged to license the label. confidence: high is not supported by a front seam that is unmarked, subordinated and catchword-crossed; lower it and mirror the row into the sidecars with a bespoke why_low_confidence naming the front-seam continuity. This is a row-field change, not a respan. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-read oshb:Isa.65.16-Isa.65.17 and confirm the row now names the byte-identical device and the connector it previously passed over; re-collate the creation runs against each other and confirm the tier written is the tier collation returns; and confirm every frame-seam claim in the row carries its quoted, tier-labelled form. No span change proposed -- whether the onset verse opens a unit at all is a boundary question and therefore boss-adoption territory, never author work.
